Name: Tony Twillie
Question: Can American golfers accomplish a sweep at this year's 2024 Open Championship?
Answer: It’s possible. 6 of the top 10 favorites to win are Americans. The last time Royal Troon hosted in 2016, Henrik Stenson won in a tight event over Phil Mickelson. Neither of them will factor in this tournament. The non-Americans in the top 10 favorites to win are formidable - McIlroy, Rahm, Aberg, and Hovland. And we know the Open Championship seems to elicit the most diverse (and maybe obtuse) champions. Todd Hamilton won here in 2004.

Name: Tony Twillie
Question: Are QB injuries in the NFL on the rise?
Answer: Yes. I think it’s a combination of things. The extra game is a small factor. Mobile QBs running the ball and getting hurt outside the pocket is also a factor. I think the biggest contributor is the emphasis on the passing game. Because there are more dropbacks now than ever, there are more opportunities for injuries to the QB. When the game was three yards and a cloud of dust, QB’s didn’t get hurt as much because they weren’t throwing as many passes. As dropbacks have increased, so have injuries. And it’s not just getting hit - several QB’s over the last few years have busted hands from hitting their hands on helmets as they passed the ball. The types of injuries run the gamut. Aaron Rodgers wasn’t hit when he popped his Achilles, but it was a pass play. Over the last 3 seasons, the number has increased exponentially. The additional game looks like cause and effect. I don’t know if that is fully accurate, but it certainly looks to be a factor. I’d like to see a couple of stats. While it would mirror the advent of the expansion of the passing game, I’d like to know how many injuries we saw when one more preseason game, more padded practices, and more live hitting in preseason. I’ve been saying this for years - the CBA that took away two-a-days and limited practice times and padded practices has softened the league. We see far too many injuries in the first month of the season because players aren’t adequately prepared to hit and be hit. And a number of the QB injuries fall into that category as well.

Name: Tony Twillie
Question: Do you think Emmitt Smith would still have dominated the league if he had an average or bad offensive line?
Answer: I think Smith would still have been a very good RB. I don’t think he’d have the most rushing yards ever without that line. I don’t know that we’d think of him as a top RB in league history without that line. With a bad line, he would have been an average RB. With an average line, he’s have been a decent RB. But in neither of those cases would we see the record broken. He wasn’t Walter Payton. Take away his big seasons with Dallas - years 2–6 when he either led the league in rushing or was close to it. Look at the seasons after that and I think you’ll get a great idea of what he’d have done. And it’s still good - for those next 6 seasons he still topped 1000 yards rushing despite the team around him becoming a bit less than it had been in the SB seasons. Probably still a HOF caliber RB. Just maybe not most rushing yards ever RB.

Name: Tony Twillie
Question: Which new pairing of coach and quarterback in the NFL for the 2024 season are you most excited to see?
Answer: There are a few intriguing combinations to look at, but I’m sure the one most people are interested in is Jim Harbaugh with Justin Herbert. Herbert has slowly developed and is already thought of as one of the more purely talented QB’s in the league. But to really make a mark, he needs to consistently make the playoffs. If Harbaugh can take Alex Smith and Colin Kaepernick to the playoffs, it stands to reason he should do it with a much more talented player in Herbert. The other big pairing many will watch is Matt Eberflus with rookie Caleb Williams; or more directly, Shane Waldron with Caleb Williams. The Bears coaching staff is on thin ice and even though they have Williams, they may not have patience to give these coaches 2 seasons to make things happen; particularly after the debacle with Justin Fields.

Name: Tony Twillie
Question: What impact do you think LSU's record-breaking performance in the SEC tournament will have on their momentum going forward?
Answer: Which one? LSU’s softball team had a pitcher throw a single SEC Tournament game record 14 innings and 208 pitches last week! That didn’t help them much as they move to super-regional play, having to go on the road to #8 Stanford for a best of 3 series this week. But I’m assuming you’re speaking of the baseball team hitting two grand slams in one game. I’ll say this - the momentum is palpable. Not only the fact that the offense woke up a bit, but also in that the pitching seems to be in post-season mode. Holman had few glitches in his game today. The Tigers only gave up one hit and they saved arms. Similarly against Georgia on Tuesday, the pitching was strong and the team jumped out to early leads in both games. It’s critical for them to find some sustained success, since this season has largely been forgettable up until the last 15 or so games of the year. And even then, they have had issues closing the deal when they needed to. They got to 13 conference wins which was the magic number to likely make it into the tournament. so they were likely already in. But playing well in Hoover affords them the opportunity to not only move up in seeding, but to gain a little confidence in themselves. How they perform in their next 2 games is critical. Win or lose, they need strong pitching performances. You’ve made it through your two regular starters, and you’re not going to see them again in Hoover, likely. It’s now time to see how deep and competent the bullpen can be. You have guys who came up big last year like Ackenhausen and Hurd who will need to find themselves again if this team is to have any real chance to compete. But make no mistake, the strong performances of Tuesday and Wednesday are a nice springboard to the post-season. And it may also catapult the team out of having to play in an unfavorable regional.
